title: Common-stage lift of supplied finite normalized tensor models
statement: Fix a prime l, a scheme X with residue-field invertibility of l, and a native realization R including its integral and common-field normalization [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data]. Fix closed, models, a symmetry and RingedDerivedTensorCoherence on the ordinary native module derived category [def-zl-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal-data]. Assume an actual family N E of CompletedTensorFiniteModel for every finite coefficient field E [def-sf-adic-completed-tensor-finite-models]. Then there is a CompletedTensorCommonLift: a natural invertible common-stage tensorator and unit with the associativity, left-unit, right-unit and signed-symmetry equations against the actual source constraints, and tensorFiniteAgreement at every E with the exact already supplied completion and ordinary comparison of N E. The ambient monoidal structure and finite normalized chain and derived comparisons are fixed inputs; this lemma constructs only their common-stage lift and its equations.

source.place: Lemma 7.9; BS Remark 6.8.15; original tensor descent steps 2--7 with the finite comparisons supplied as input.

proof_origin.place: Definition 3.4.10, Remark 6.8.15; HRS Lemma 7.9. Agent-written normalization and finite common-field argument, retained from the original node.

proof.text: For each E, invert exactly (N E).completion.comparison on constructible pairs using its normalized final clause. Compose its image under native derived scalar extension with (N E).ordinary inverse and conjugate by R.integral. This gives the finite tensorator on integral representatives; the defining composite is precisely tensorFiniteAgreement. The normalization and representative square of N identify this map on simultaneous K-flat models, without choosing an unrelated tensorator.

On coherent reductions, completedPrimitiveCounitComparison and normalized DVR effectivity identify the completed constraints with their whole-system tensor maps. NormalizedTensorConstraintTransport identifies reassociation, both actions and signed swap even when an inner tensor is re-resolved. IntegralAmbientOperationModels identifies the quotient augmentation with that of (N E).completion, including its zero shifted coordinate. To compare the possibly different ordinary tensor presentations, whisker with the two good-complex localizations and their supplied model isomorphisms. The representative equations identify both maps there; fully faithful whiskering then identifies the descended natural transformations. The balanced pure generators likewise determine the cochain comparison. Thus arbitrary supplied N give the same normalized finite maps. Combining these squares with the supplied native coherence proves the four finite constraint equations.

For E contained in F, insert the specified inverse finite-free completion comparison. ScalarExtensionTowerCoherence identifies the tensor comparison with the balanced whole-tower map. After the augmentations from step 1 both routes multiply the same scalars. Thus the finite tensorators agree under R.common_field, including identity and successive extensions, even for ramified fields.

Localize the integral Hom modules. Pure rational arrows u tensor a and v tensor b multiply the integral naturality square by ab; additivity and balancing treat all arrows. The inverse components localize too. The finite constraint and scalar squares remain equalities after localization.

For two common-stage objects choose a finite field containing their stages. Use the localized comparison there and conjugate by the actual stage-inclusion and R.common_field comparisons. Step 3 proves independence under further extension; any two choices admit a common further field. Represent two arrows at one further field and use step 4 to prove naturality, independent of arrow representatives. The same construction on inverse components proves invertibility.

Every constraint diagram is represented at one common finite field. Steps 2--4 prove its equality there and step 5 identifies its edges with the common tensorator. For the unit use coefficient multiplication, whose inverse inserts one. Its two action equations follow from the same finite balanced maps. The formula of step 1 at each E is the integral_tensor field. Empty X, zero complexes, identity field extensions and odd-degree swaps require no different construction.
